html:
Czechoslovakia was a state in central Europe from 1918 to 1992, joining the Czechs of Bohemia and Moravia with the Slovaks. It was made from the ruins of Austria-Hungary at the end of the First World War, under its founding president Tomáš Garrigue Masaryk.

Between the wars it was the one lasting democracy in central Europe, and an industrial one. It held a large German minority in the Sudetenland. In 1938 Britain and France accepted Hitler's demand for that land in the Munich Agreement, and in March 1939 Germany occupied the rest.

Rebuilt in 1945, it expelled most of its Germans, and in 1948 the communists seized power. In 1968 the Prague Spring tried "socialism with a human face" until Warsaw Pact tanks crushed it. The peaceful Velvet Revolution of 1989 made the playwright Václav Havel president. On 1 January 1993 the country split peacefully into the Czech Republic and Slovakia.
